newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Currency woes continue to spook Singapore shares.
newsitem.headline: Currency woes continue to spook Singapore shares.

text.p: The Singapore stock market remained a bear den on Tuesday as Asian currency volatility blunted fund interest and pushed the key share index down to another new 30-month low at mid-morning.

"The market is spooked by recent currency attacks. While the Singapore dollar is unlikely to suffer from an attack, people are nearvous and watching how the other currencies will impact its stability," said a local dealer.
Southeast Asian currencies, including Malaysia's ringgit, have been battered by heavy selling against the U.S. dollar following the de facto devaluation of the peso and the baht earlier this month.
After hitting a low of 1,944.64, the Straits Times Industrials Index was at 1,946.81, down 7.79 points at 0150 GMT.
It was dragged down by index-linked food firm Cerebos, car firm Cycle & Carriage and Singapore Airlines.
"It's not time to buy yet. We are expecting the index to test 1,900 in the next couple of weeks. At that level, it should begin to stabilize," said a dealer with a European institution.
Electronic shares bucked the trend. The SES electronics index was up 1.24 points at 132.35, led by multimedia Creative Technology, which rose S$1.30 to S$29.40 following gains in the United States.
Trade in Malaysian shares was thin amid nervousness over the weak ringgit and higher interest rates.
"The benefit of a weaker ringgit to the stocks market is being offset by a higher interest rate. Funds will sell," said another dealer with a European institution.
Dealers said investors were unhappy that Malaysia would allow market forces to determine the value of the ringgit.
"It would mean losing some of the ringgit's value. That's no good for investors," the dealer siad.
The UOB OTC index hit a new low of 1,092.67, down 3.44 points.
Total market volume was 18.6 million shares with 27 gainers to 125 gainers.
